title: Prove a goal builds to completion: a 3-node graph, staffed in parallel, landed on one goal
description:
SPIDR child 5 of parent task-4423d2a4c3084d579c132b253d36b502 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-04). THE HARDENING AND PROOF ROW for this parent - it owns the e2e, the live drive, the docs sweep and the adversarial pass for the whole multi-node feature, so no sibling child files its own evidence row (global rail 21).

dependsOn ALL four production children plus the leaf; each is named because this row certifies the capability THEY shipped (global rail 4 clause 2):
- task-6c05745519844bf39cdebca6d75bb72a - EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT discloses observedVersion (a real seat can release; without it the second seat's claim lapses at the 30-min TTL and the live drive stalls).
- task-f79d38b119984ae1ae51eba887a28b7d - the compiler seals N nodes.
- task-1d7b9df2579c491992b55de791c99f4f - a node is READY only when its HARD dependencies are ACCEPTED.
- task-92d84d384e4443d7bf78c76024af5688 - parallel seats + the disclosed concurrency limit.
- task-0b26dc9e8582428ea1af8032d9277550 - the status strip's coverage words.

WHAT THIS ROW PROVES: the parent's headline claim - a goal is built to completion as ONE goal, not one node at a time and not through a successor goal. Per owner ruling comment-fbe64776 the growth path is the sealed multi-node INITIAL graph, NOT graph.request_expansion; the parent's DoD 2 phrase "expansion run" reads as "the sealed multi-node INITIAL graph" throughout.

MEASURED CONTEXT (branch moe/work-2026-09-04, by architect-20a6d1eb):
- e2e lanes exist: `tests/e2e/foundation` and `tests/e2e/control-room`; `package.json:21` `test:e2e` = `tsc -p tests/e2e/foundation/tsconfig.json && vitest run tests/e2e`, and `:22` `test:e2e:browser` drives playwright.
- README still asserts the retired rule ("an initial plan seals one node, so a goal is built one node at a time and growth goes through a successor goal"). That sentence is now false and this row rewrites it.
- REPLAN stays as-is for exhausted reviews: `apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/replan-successor-port.ts` is NOT retired by this work; only the claim that growth REQUIRES a successor goal is.
- The live lane recipe and its pitfalls are in memories control-room-live-lane-recipe and productize-loop-2026-09-03; the UnAI goal is goal-c9d9850b at `D:/projexts/UnAI/.moe-next/store.sqlite`.
definitionOfDone: OFFLINE e2e over a REAL daemon (no fixtures, real MCP wire, scripted seat double): one goal, ONE approval decision, a sealed 3-node graph with a HARD chain. Assert IN ORDER: node count = 3 on the sealed graph; the two independent nodes are BOTH staffed in one pass while the dependent node is BLOCKED on `depends:`; the dependent node is staffed only after its parent is ACCEPTED; all three deliver, verify and land on the SAME goalRef.

The coverage read is the closing gate: `POST /documents/coverage/read` reports every approved criterion VERIFIED and the goal reaches ready-to-close ONLY then. Assert a NEGATIVE arm in the same test - at 2 of 3 nodes accepted the goal is NOT ready to close - so the gate is not vacuously green.

NO SUCCESSOR GOAL was minted for growth: the e2e asserts exactly ONE goal aggregate exists at the end and that no replan/successor path was taken. Assert by counting goal aggregates in the store, not by the absence of a log line.

LIVE DRIVE on the lane (UnAI at D:/projexts/UnAI, goal-c9d9850b or a fresh goal): a multi-node graph proposed by a real planning seat, approved in the BROWSER, and at least two nodes landed on the same goal. Record in a row comment (each under 4500 chars): the transcript, the store path, and the landing shas. Never restart the wrapper to unstick a seat - claim TTL is 30 min.

README's "one node at a time / growth goes through a successor goal" sentence is rewritten to the measured truth (an initial plan seals the whole DAG; independent nodes build in parallel up to the seat limit; REPLAN remains the path for an exhausted review). `git grep -n "one node at a time"` returns 0 hits in docs.

Adversarial pass over the whole parent's diff, recorded in a step note, answering at minimum: what happens when two wrapper passes race on the same READY node; what happens when a dependency's review is unreadable rather than accepted or rejected; what a cycle in dependsOn does (it must refuse at compile, not deadlock the surface); and what an operator sees when the seat limit is 1.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e`. State explicitly that `pnpm test` covers no apps/** (global rail 18), and attribute any foreign red by the merge-base/HEAD delta (global rail 3).
taskRails: This row RUNS the proof; it does not re-implement the feature. If an e2e arm fails because a sibling child under-delivered, comment on THAT row and report blocked on it - do not patch the production surface here (global rail 4: a proof that reimplements authority inside the test retires the question unanswered).

NO FIXTURE-BACKED JOURNEY. The parent rail demands a REAL daemon and a real MCP wire; a mock-backed e2e does not discharge DoD 2. If the seat double cannot drive the real wire, report blocked rather than substituting fixtures.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited from the parent): the verifier stays the documented trusted-workspace v0.1 limitation. No signing, hermetic verification or freeze manifests.
Never restart the wrapper to unstick a seat (claim TTL 30 min; memory real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04). Read the latest WorkClaimed payload's expiresAt from the store and wait.

implementationPlan.description: TEACH THE REAL-PROCESS HARNESS A MULTI-NODE GRAPH. tests/e2e/foundation/j1-loop-harness.ts (412 lines) already spawns a REAL daemon, wrapper and agent: `startDaemon` (:200), `runSeed` (:235), `writeAgentShim(scratch, arm)` (:310), `runWrapper`/`spawnWrapper` (:340/:349), with `NODE_REF = SEEDED_LOW_RISK_TASK.nodeRef` (:50) — ONE node today. Extend it, do not fork it: seed a goal whose approved contract has criteria split across THREE nodes with a HARD chain. THE SHAPE IS LOAD-BEARING: make two nodes INDEPENDENT of each other and the third dependent on one of them. A straight a->b->c chain would make the parallel-staffing arm unreachable, and three independent nodes would make the blocking arm unreachable; this shape exercises both in one graph. Add an `AgentArm` value that delivers whichever node the wrapper staffs it onto, so one shim serves all three. Keep every existing arm and its behaviour untouched — j1-loop-real-process.e2e.test.ts's three arms must stay green with unchanged counts, and step 7 compares them.

implementationPlan.description: THE E2E, in a NEW file over the REAL daemon and the real MCP wire with NO fixtures (task rail 2 — a mock-backed journey does not discharge DoD 1, and if the shim cannot drive the real wire, report blocked rather than substituting fixtures). ONE goal, ONE approval decision, a sealed 3-node graph. Assert IN ORDER, each against durable state rather than log text: (a) the sealed graph carries exactly 3 execution-bearing nodes; (b) on the first staffing pass the TWO independent nodes are BOTH spawned while the dependent node's step reports BLOCKED with `depends:<nodeKey>` — assert both spawns by work-item id and the blocked token literally; (c) the dependent node is staffed only on a pass AFTER its parent's review is accepted; (d) all three deliver, verify and land against the SAME goalRef.
implementationPlan.note:
THE E2E EXISTS AND IS GREEN, NO FIXTURES: `tests/e2e/foundation/multi-node-graph.e2e.test.ts` (270 lines, 3 arms). `npx vitest run tests/e2e/foundation/multi-node-graph.e2e.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 3 passed (3)`, THREE consecutive rolls (28.62s / 30.47s / stable), so the concurrency sampler is not a flake.

WHAT IS REAL. `daemon-main.ts` is spawned as its own OS process on an ephemeral port and every journey command goes over ITS OWN HTTP `/command` route with the SHIPPED runtime envelope (`toWireEnvelope`). `agent-wrapper-main.ts` is spawned as its own process, hosts the REAL MCP server, and the seat double talks JSON-RPC to it over that wire (`initialize` -> `work_get_context` -> `review_submit` -> `work_release`). The daemon's OWN verifier runs each node's test as a child. NOTHING is faked: no fixture store, no stub surface, no in-process shortcut for anything the seat touches. Task rail 2 is satisfied without a substitution, so no block was needed.

THE ONE THING NOT ON THE WIRE, stated plainly: the durable HUMAN principal is minted by calling the PRODUCTION port `/session/pair/open` composes (`provider.pairingOpenSessions().createPrincipal`), because the browser reaches it by SIGNING an Ed25519 pairing challenge — an authentication transport this row does not certify, and re-implementing one security handshake in a test is how the weaker copy becomes the real bound. The Gate 1 approval ITSELF still travels the real HTTP wire under that principal's session credential, with the daemon-minted bearer presentation. `compiled-product-journey.test.ts:158-166` mints it the same way.

THE JOURNEY (the real product path a planning seat uses, not the demo seed's):
  world prelude (the SHIPPED `buildDemoSeedPlan`, sliced at goal.create BY KIND, plus `policy.validate`)
  -> goal.create_with_source: ONE goal bound to ONE PRD
  -> product_contract.propose_revision (AGENT session): three criteria
  -> product_contract.approve_gate_1 (HUMAN session, daemon-minted template)
  -> planning.submit_decomposition (AGENT session): the 3-node DAG. The DAEMON compiles it via
     `compiledPlanAuthority` and drives create/ready/claim/propose/finalize itself, so this row
     composes ZERO authority bytes (global rail 4: no authority reimplemented in the test).
  -> approval.decide_intent (HUMAN session): THE ONE PLAN-APPROVAL DECISION, and it seals all three.

THE ASSERTIONS, IN THE DoD'S ORDER, each against durable state:
(a) EXACTLY 3 execution-bearing nodes WITH the hard chain, read off the sealed graph's own edges through the production `activeCompiledGraphs`: `toEqual([{dependsOn:[],nodeKey:node-alpha},{dependsOn:[],nodeKey:node-beta},{dependsOn:[node-alpha,node-beta],nodeKey:node-omega}])`, every goalRef = goal-multi-1. Not a count — the SHAPE.
(b) BOTH INDEPENDENT NODES IN ONE PASS, by WORK-ITEM ID from `workItemIdFor` (never a hand-written literal): `claimedWorkItems` after pass 1 `toEqual([node.deliver@node-alpha, node.deliver@node-beta])` and `.not.toContain(node.deliver@node-omega)`. Claims are the durable fold, committed BEFORE the spawn, so this is falsifiable where the pass report is not. AND AT THE SAME MOMENT: `openClaimWatcher` samples the claim register every 40ms DURING the pass and one sample held BOTH work items OPEN simultaneously — the fact a staff-wait-staff loop cannot produce. Its own positive control (`samples.filter(held => held.length > 0).length > 0`) is asserted FIRST so a watcher that could only ever say "nothing held" satisfies nothing.
    THE BLOCKED TOKEN LITERALLY, with its node suffix: `dependsTokens(step.missing) toEqual ["depends:node-alpha","depends:node-beta"]`. Prefix-only would stay green if the surface named the wrong producers (task-0b26dc9e's `waiting` fold keys on the PREFIX because the token carries a suffix — so the suffix is exactly what needed pinning here).
(c) THE DEPENDENT NODE ONLY AFTER ACCEPTANCE: asserted three ways. Before ANY staffing the omega step is BLOCKED; after pass 1 it is still unclaimed and undelivered (`delivered(scratch, OMEGA) toBeNull`); only after both producers are ACCEPTED does the surface read READY and pass 2 claim it.
(d) ALL THREE DELIVER, VERIFY AND LAND ON THE SAME goalRef. Delivery: each node's OWN workspace holds its own `math.mjs`. Verification: the daemon's verifier accepted each (the coverage read below is downstream of that acceptance). LANDING IS LITERAL — each node's own git history carries `Moe landed node <nodeRef> after the daemon verified it.`, read with `git log --format=%B` from the workspace.

implementationPlan.description: THE CLOSING GATE AND ITS NEGATIVE ARM, in the same new e2e file. (a) `POST /documents/coverage/read` reports every approved criterion VERIFIED once all three nodes are accepted, and the goal reaches ready-to-close only then. (b) THE NEGATIVE ARM, in the same test rather than a separate one so it cannot drift: at two-of-three nodes accepted the goal is NOT ready to close and coverage is short by exactly the third node's criteria — assert the verified/criteria numbers, not merely a boolean, because a gate asserted only in its satisfied state is vacuous (global rail 1). (c) NO SUCCESSOR GOAL WAS MINTED: assert the store holds exactly ONE goal aggregate at the end, counted from durable state — not inferred from the absence of a log line, which would pass on a store where nothing ran at all. This is the assertion that actually proves the parent's headline claim, that growth no longer requires a successor goal.
implementationPlan.note:
THE CLOSING GATE, ITS NEGATIVE ARM AND THE ONE-GOAL COUNT — all three in the SAME `it()` as steps 3's assertions, so they cannot drift apart. Green: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 3 passed (3)`.

(a) THE GATE, SATISFIED. `POST /documents/coverage/read {goalRef}` after all three nodes are accepted: `full.totals toEqual {criteria: 3, planned: 0, verified: 3}` and every criterion row's `status` is `VERIFIED` (checked per row, not just via the total). Ready-to-close is asserted through the PRODUCTION derivation, not a boolean of mine: `goalCloseReadinessFor(store, projectId, goalId) toEqual {criteria: 3, kind: "READY"}` — and the surface then offers `goal.close`. The daemon's own `closeReadiness` port (`affordance-read.ts:272`) is the same call, so this is the value the browser reads.

(b) THE NEGATIVE ARM, in the same test, at exactly two of three accepted (after pass 1, before pass 2):
      partial.totals toEqual { criteria: 3, planned: 1, verified: 2 }
      VERIFIED criterion ids toEqual ["crit-alpha", "crit-beta"]     <- WHICH two, not just how many
      closeReadiness toEqual { criteria: 3, kind: "NOT_READY", verified: 2 }
    NUMBERS, never a boolean: `NOT_READY` alone cannot tell 2-of-3 from 0-of-3, and a gate asserted only in its satisfied state is vacuous (global rail 1). One criterion per node is what makes the shortfall EXACTLY the third node's criterion rather than an unattributed remainder.

(c) NO SUCCESSOR GOAL. `goalAggregates(scratch) toEqual ["goal-multi-1"]` — COUNTED from the durable fold, using the SAME shape `activeCompiledGraphs` uses to recognise a goal (a folded record whose own `goalId` is its aggregate id, scoped to the project), so "one goal" means here exactly what the production walk means by it. Plus `[...new Set(sealedNodes().map(n => n.goalRef))] toEqual ["goal-multi-1"]`: all three nodes belong to that one goal. Neither reads a log line — an absence-of-REPLAN assertion would read green on a store where nothing ever ran, which is the failure mode the plan named.

MUTATION DRILL ON THE GATE, run and RED — and it is the NEGATIVE arm that catches it, which is the whole point. Target `apps/daemon/src/http/document-coverage-read.ts:228`: `facts?.accepted !== undefined ? "VERIFIED" : "PLANNED"` -> `"VERIFIED"`, i.e. a coverage read that calls every planned criterion verified regardless of acceptance. Result: RED at the two-of-three arm with `{criteria: 3, planned: 0, verified: 3}` against the expected `{criteria: 3, planned: 1, verified: 2}`. THE SATISFIED 3-of-3 ARM STAYED GREEN UNDER THIS MUTATION — direct evidence that without the negative arm this gate would certify a goal it never measured.

comments.content:
STEP 7(b) — ADVERSARIAL PASS over the WHOLE parent feature's diff (all five children; this row owns it, global rail 21). Every answer is MEASURED at HEAD, with the file and line that decides it.

Q1. TWO WRAPPER PASSES RACE ON THE SAME READY NODE — IS THE CLAIM THE ONLY FENCE?
NO. There are FOUR, and three of them are durable. `createAgentSessionFence.admit` (`agent-session-fence.ts:191-227`) checks, IN ORDER:
  1. the durable WORK CLAIM (`activeClaim`) -> `AGENT_STAFFING_CLAIM_HELD`;
  2. the durable LIVE-CHILD staffing record, which fences a claim that EXPIRED while the child still runs -> `AGENT_STAFFING_CHILD_LIVE`;
  3. an OS liveness probe of that record's `childPid`, which fences an unretired record left by a SIGKILLed wrapper.
Plus the wrapper's own pre-checks (`agent-wrapper.ts:353` `step.claim !== null`, `:356` `staffing.has(workItemId)`).
EVERY unknown FAILS CLOSED WITH ITS OWN CODE: a corrupt claim ledger or unreadable staffing record answers `AGENT_STAFFING_RECORD_UNREADABLE` ("a corrupt claim ledger must never read as 'nobody holds it'"), and a probe outage answers a DISTINCT `AGENT_STAFFING_LIVENESS_UNKNOWN` so it is never mistaken for ordinary contention.
THE TOCTOU that remains is closed one layer down, not by `admit`: `admit` READS, then the caller COMMITS. Two wrappers can both pass `admit`. The commit is version-fenced — `agent-wrapper.ts:256-257` dispatches `work.claim` at `step.claimAggregateVersion`, and the fence's own `append` commits at `expectedVersion: store.getAggregateVersion(aggregateId)` — so the loser takes EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT and spawns nothing. NET: two seats cannot both run one node; the losing pass reports a coded refusal rather than silently double-staffing.

Q2. A DEPENDENCY WHOSE REVIEW IS UNREADABLE RATHER THAN ACCEPTED OR REJECTED — BLOCK OR LEAK?
IT BLOCKS. `isAccepted` (`affordance-read.ts:387-394`) is `readReviewLedger(...).accepted !== undefined`, and an unreadable ledger sets `unreadable: true` while LEAVING `accepted` undefined (`review-read-model.ts:231/237/255` — a malformed round is never partly trusted). So the consumer's `unmet` list keeps naming it and the node stays BLOCKED. The unreadable node's OWN step also blocks: `awaitingVerify = review.unreadable || latestRound?.routing.route === "ACCEPT"` (`affordance-read.ts:409`). NO LEAK in either direction.
THE GAP, and it is real: the consumer is told `depends:<nodeKey>` — the SAME token as "not finished yet". An unreadable producer is therefore indistinguishable from an unfinished one, and the goal waits forever on a message that says nothing is wrong. Fail-closed but NOT DIAGNOSABLE. Follow-up A below; not patched here (task rail 1).

Q3. A dependsOn CYCLE — DOES IT SEAL AND DEADLOCK?
NO. IT REFUSES AT COMPILE, and the answer is a SURVIVING COMMITTED ARM, not a transcript: `apps/daemon/src/planning/compile-dispatcher.test.ts:134` "refuses a dependsOn CYCLE, which only a multi-node graph can express" asserts `COMPILED_PLAN_ADMISSION_REFUSED @ COMPILED_PLAN_PRODUCER` for a<->b plus c->b, AND `store.getAggregateVersion(RUN_ID)).toBe(0)` — nothing sealed. Its own comment names exactly the hazard this question asks about: "a cycle that SEALED would deadlock the dependency gate rather than refuse at the surface: no node is ever READY." A cycle clears every `shapeRefusal` arm (no unknown target, no self-edge, nothing depends on the completion node) and is caught deeper by the graph codec. NO FOLLOW-UP ROW NEEDED — the gate cannot deadlock because the cycle never reaches it.

Q4. WHAT DOES AN OPERATOR SEE WITH THE SEAT LIMIT AT 1?
Two DIFFERENT facts, and the surface keeps them apart — now pinned by a COMMITTED arm in this row's e2e ("staffs one independent node and leaves the other READY, offered and unclaimed"):
  - the unstaffed INDEPENDENT node stays `READY` and still carries its `review.submit` offer: work waiting on a SEAT;
  - the DEPENDENT node is `BLOCKED` with `depends:<nodeKey>`: work waiting on the GRAPH.
In words, `seatLimitWords` (`activity-words.ts:125-133`) says: "This daemon is set to run 1 agent at once. Every seat is busy, so the next ready node waits for one to finish." Correct and unambiguous. That arm is ALSO the positive control for the two-seat parallel arm: same graph, only the limit moves.

Q5. DOES ANYTHING DOWNSTREAM STILL ASSUME ONE NODE PER SEALED GRAPH?
YES — THREE places. All three FAIL CLOSED with a named code or an empty answer; none mis-activates a multi-node graph, and none is on the lane this row proved (the e2e sealed, activated, staffed, verified, landed and closed a 3-node graph end to end, so every one of these is off that path):
